children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Intercontinental Exchange canola futures were declining Wednesday but had come away from their session lows.
An analyst said canola ran into resistance when it peaked above C$840 per metric ton and then fell back with weaker crude oil prices.
However, crude has since turned modestly higher with canola softening its losses.
The analyst said canola has support at C$810 per metric ton, but if crude oil prices tumble, and with harvest pressure, falling below C$800 is possible.

However, given the current situation in the Middle East, he doesn't expect crude or the harvest to have much of a negative impact. The analyst said the outlook for canola is positive with good demand expected through 2026-27 marketing year.
Among the veg oils, the Chicago soy complex was lower, with sharp losses in soyoil. European rapeseed was to the downside but Malaysian palm oil was tacking on small increases.
Manitoba reported its canola harvest was 5% complete with the provincewide harvest of all crops pegged at 11% done.
Following the latest Bank of Canada interest rate freeze, the Canadian dollar move higher. The loonie climbed to 72.22 U.S. cents late Wednesday morning, compared with Tuesday's close of 71.96.
